messages.subject: [STATSGRASS] grass.itc.it server migration to new machine
messages.subject_clean: [STATSGRASS] grass.itc.it server migration to new machine
messages.body_plain:
Dear GRASS community,

this week we want to migrate 'grass.itc.it' to a new
machine. It is likely that the server is down for
1 hour (maybe less, maybe more). The basic problem
is the migration of all mailing lists which requires
to stop the email server for the time of migration.

ITC-irst continues to support the GRASS project.
The good old server is up for 448 days now; we hope
that the new server behaves as well as the old one.

Additional change: Once the new machine is up (same
name, same IP), I want to migrate the GRASS User list
(kindly hosted at Baylor University) to our server to
get control over it. Currently we cannot help with
subsciption issues etc. The plan is to fully enable
the already existing GRASS User list which runs in
background for some years now (to maintain the list
archive - at Baylor no archive are provided). I'll
transfer all subscribers to the IRST based user list,
you will then receive an announcement with password.
Mails to the old Baylor address should still arrive
as our list here is subscribed as user there. Nothing
should get lost.

We try to miminize the outage time and we will announce
once the new server is up & running.

Best regards

 Markus

--
Markus Neteler     <neteler itc it>       http://mpa.itc.it
ITC-irst -  Centro per la Ricerca Scientifica e Tecnologica
MPBA - Predictive Models for Biol. & Environ. Data Analysis
Via Sommarive, 18        -       38050 Povo (Trento), Italy

messages.subject: [STATSGRASS] mode in R
messages.body_plain:
On Tue, 23 May 2006, Carlos "Gu?no" Grohmann wrote:

> This should be really silly, but if I have a raster map that I loaded
> into R, how can I get the mode of the raster values?

If the raster is a CELL, that is integer or categorical, you can tabulate 
the unique values (but even so, there may be multiple modes). If it is 
FCELL or DCELL, the mode is not well defined, because it depends on the 
resolution of your observations on the real line. There have been several 
discussions of this on R-help, see RSiteSearch("mode") or in particular 
the thread including:

http://finzi.psych.upenn.edu/R/Rhelp02a/archive/13990.html

using kernel densities to attack the problem.

Roger
